principles: Lattice is the only active runtime and documentation name.
Compatibility deletion must be mechanically tested, not just hidden from help text.
Historical signed data is preserved unless it is active runtime compatibility.
Keep the change scoped to entrypoints, generated assets, adapter checks, active docs, and tests.
drivers: User explicitly does not need koala compatibility.
Current help and runtime checks still advertise and accept legacy alias paths.
Leaving fallback binaries alive would contradict the desired lattice-only product surface.

options.name: A: Remove only user-visible help wording
pros: Immediately removes the exact annoying terminal text
cons: Leaves koala wrappers, fallbacks, docs, and tests alive
Future tests could still preserve compatibility contrary to user intent

options.name: B: Remove active runtime compatibility and update docs/tests, preserve immutable historical records
pros: Gives tests a clear absence contract
Avoids corrupting signed or historical process data
cons: Touches more files than a wording-only patch
Requires careful classification of koala references

options.name: C: Rename or delete every koala token in the repository
pros: No grep hits for koala in active tree if fully successful
cons: High risk of breaking signed evidence, process lane names, archived docs, and unrelated history
Large noisy diff with low product value

chosen: B: Remove active runtime compatibility and update docs/tests, preserve immutable historical records
rationale: Option B is the smallest implementation that satisfies the user-facing requirement and prevents the old alias from silently returning. It removes active compatibility while avoiding destructive historical rewrites.

preMortem.scenario: A stale bin/koala.js wrapper still exists after the change
preMortem.trigger: Generated asset logic keeps legacy path selection or verification accepts old wrappers
preMortem.consequence: The exact compatibility the user asked to delete remains usable
preMortem.mitigation: Remove legacy wrapper generation and update Codex/entrypoint verification to require lattice-only wrappers.

preMortem.scenario: Tests pass because they only stop checking the alias wording
preMortem.trigger: Compatibility smokes are deleted without replacement absence assertions
preMortem.consequence: A later refactor can reintroduce koala fallback unnoticed
preMortem.mitigation: Rewrite smokes and verification scripts to assert koala runtime alias/fallback is absent.

preMortem.scenario: Historical/process data is renamed too aggressively
preMortem.trigger: A global search-replace changes signed story data or old reviewer lane identifiers
preMortem.consequence: Existing evidence validation or audit trails become invalid
preMortem.mitigation: Classify each koala reference and exclude immutable historical evidence or process identifiers from the compatibility deletion.
